messages:
Alex (AE): quick heads-up — ACME POC hit a spend alert and their free credits dropped to 0 mid-demo. They saw 429s and the app froze. Can someone triage? :grimacing:
Meera (Solutions): ugh. Do we have the account id / org? what endpoints were they hitting?@Jordan (Billing) tagging you for visibility :eyes:
Alex (AE): acct=acct-ACME-001, env=sandbox. They were doing a demo with streaming chat + background embedding of docs. Console shows ~1.2M tokens in last 30m; SDK debug shows ~600k.
Sam (SRE): got it. Can you paste the client request logs / snippet? Curious about retries or duped requests on network flaps. Also any rate-limit 429 bodies?
Alex (AE): here's the debug they sent (redacted):
```
// pseudo-code
const client = new RedwoodClient({apiKey: process.env.RW});
// stream chat
client.chat.stream({model:'rw-large', messages})
// simultaneously index docs
client.embeddings.create({model:'embed-1', input: docs})
// network retry wrapper that re-sends if socket closes
```
They said the demo machine had intermittent wifi drops.
Jordan (Billing): billing-bot logs: spend_alert triggered at 1845678800 UTC for acct-ACME-001; free_credits_consumed=1,200,432 tokens; remaining_free=0. I'll hold off final invoicing while we triage. Do you want to apply a safety credit? :thinking_face:
Sam (SRE): initial hunch — duplicates from the retry wrapper + streaming semantics. Streaming reconnects can re-send first chunk without an idempotency key and our meter counts each chunk as new tokens. We have a shortcoming where non-idempotent client retries can double-count if the client doesn't set X-Request-ID / idempotency-key.
Meera (Solutions): possible mitigation to give customer: 1) temporarily increase free credits or apply ad-hoc credit, 2) ask them to set a unique request id header on each logical call, 3) turn off concurrent embed flow during the demo. Jordan, can you grant a small one-off?
Jordan (Billing): I can add a 150k token credit to sandbox acct while we investigate. Doing that now. Will also mute spend alerts for 1 hour to let them finish the demo.
Alex (AE): thanks — customer is ok with a patch. They want a short explanation we can share with their infra folks.
Sam (SRE): follow-up from logs — pasted extracted lines:
```
metering: acct=acct-ACME-001 req_id= null tokens=120034
metering: acct=acct-ACME-001 req_id= null tokens=119984
stream: reconnect attempt=1 bytes=4096
stream: reconnect attempt=2 bytes=4096
```
Note req_id null on repeated chunks. We should dedupe at ingest by client-provided id or by a short-time-window session-hash.
Meera (Solutions): can you draft 2 bullets we can send to customer (what happened + immediate steps)
Sam (SRE): draft: "We observed duplicate token ingestion caused by client-side retrying of streaming chunks without a stable request id. Tokens were counted on reconnects. Immediate mitigations: add a unique X-Request-ID header for each logical operation, avoid simultaneous heavy embed runs during live demos, and we've applied a temporary credit while we fix server-side deduping."
Alex (AE): paste that to customer now. Also cc'ing their infra lead.
Jordan (Billing): FYI I posted the 150k credit and muted the alert at 1845679005. billing-bot confirms: {event:credit_adjustment, amount:150000, reason:"POC support - demo interruption"}.
billing-bot: Credit adjustment recorded for acct-ACME-001: +150000 tokens.
Meera (Solutions): what's the long-term fix? timeline?
Sam (SRE): plan: (1) short-term patch to honor client-provided idempotency header (PR queued) — ETA 3hrs, (2) add server-side 60s window dedupe keyed by stream session hash — ETA 3 days, (3) update docs and our quickstart with a recommended X-Request-ID pattern — ETA 1 day. I'll open ticket RW-POC-233 in backlog and link PRs.
Alex (AE): customer grateful. They asked we follow up with a short postmortem and that their demo credit be reflected in the invoice. Jordan, can you confirm billing notes?
Jordan (Billing): noted on the acct; will annotate invoice with demo credit and make sure no surprise charges. I'll also whitelist sandbox for one more demo on Tuesday if they want to retest.
Sam (SRE): deployed the idempotency header acceptance in canary at 1845679100. Early metrics show duplicate token events down ~92% in the test harness. Monitoring for the next 4h.
Alex (AE): excellent. Customer restarted demo and finished successfully. They logged a follow-up ask to have a best-practice snippet in our docs.
Meera (Solutions): I'll add a short recipe to the POC playbook and link the doc in the follow-up email.
Alex (AE): closing the loop with ACME and sending a wrap email. Thanks team :raised_hands:
Sam (SRE): leaving this thread open for 24h to monitor, will close after no regressions. :thumbsup:
